THE GENERAL DEPARTMENT OF POST AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
CIRCULAR No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD OF SEPTEMBER 29, 2000 GUIDING THE ACTIVITIES REGARDING THE CONDITIONAL BUSINESS LINES IN THE DOMAINS
OF POST, TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND INTERNET

In furtherance of the provisions of Decree No. 03/2000/ND-CP of February 3, 2000 guiding the implementation of a number of articles
of the Enterprises Law and Decree No. 30/2000/ND-CP of August 11, 2000 on the cancellation of a number of permits and licenses and
the conversion of a number of licenses into business conditions and, at the same time, in order to create favorable conditions for
activities of enterprises; after consulting with several concerned ministries and branches, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
hereby guides a number of contents of business activities in the domains of post, telecommunications and internet as follows:
I. GENERAL PROVISIONS


1.1 This Circular provides guidance for enterprises engaged in business activities in the domain of post and telecommunications and
Internet, as prescribed by law, which fall under the conditional business lines.
1.2 Post and/or telecommunications enterprises are enterprises engaged in business activities in one or several domains prescribed
in the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on post and telecommunications. The conditional post and telecommunication
business lines include:
a/ Provision of postal and telecommunication services;
b/ Manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;


c/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Printing of postage stamps; production, import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage
stamps.
1.3 Internet services-providing enterprises are enterprises dealing in Internet services specified in the Government�s Decree No.
21/CP of March 5, 1997 issuing the Provisional Regulation on the management, establishment and use of the Internet in Vietnam".
The conditional Internet business lines include:
a/ Provision of Internet access services (IAP);
b/ Provision of Internet services (ISP).


1.4 The postal, telecommunication and Internet domains fall under the conditional business lines, where some business domains require
permits of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications while some others do not but must satisfy the conditions set in
this Circular.
1.5 Various kinds of permits and certificates used for technical and professional management prescribed in Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP
in order to ensure the network and service quality, ensure safety for operation of public and exclusive postal and telecommunication
networks and ensure the interests of users shall not be regulated by this Circular.


II. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE PERMITS
2.1 The post, telecommunication and Internet business lines that require permits include:
a/ Establishment of national telecommunication backbone networks, public telecommunication networks and provision (direct or for resale)
of telecommunication services (basic, value-added);
b/ Establishment of Internet networks and provision of Internet services (IAP and ISP);
c/ Establishment of postal networks and provision of postal services;
d/ Printing of postage stamps;
e/ Manufacture of radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters.


2.2. Enterprises conducting business activities in the domains specified at Points a, b, c and d, Section 2.1 shall be State enterprises
or joint-stock companies where the State holds the predominant or special shares. For the domain specified at Point e, Section 2.1,
the business subjects shall be enterprises of any economic sector. Enterprises may do business in these domains under conditions
and according to the operating duration specified in their permits and start their business activities only when they obtain their
licenses.


2.3. Enterprises must make business registration according to law provisions before carrying out procedures applying for permits to
do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above.
2.4. The conditions, order and procedures for granting of permits to do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above shall
be as follows:
a/ For permits stated at Point a , the provisions in Circular No. 04/1998/TT-TCBD of September 29, 1998 of the General Department
of Post and Telecommunications guiding the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on telecommunication networks
and services, shall be complied with.


b/ For permits specified at Point b, the provisions of Joint Circular No. 08/TTLT of May 24, 197 of the General Department of Post
and Telecommunications, the Ministry of the Interior (now the Ministry of Public Security) and the Ministry of Culture and Information
guiding the licensing of the connection, provision and use of Internet in Vietnam, shall be complied with;


c/ For permits specified at Point c, the provisions of Circular No. 02/1998/TT-TCBD of June 20, 1998 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications guiding the implementation of the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP on postal networks and services,
shall be complied with;
d/ For permits specified at Point d, the provisions of Decision No. 217/2000/QD-TCBD of March 6, 2000 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications issuing the Regulation on the professional management of postage stamps, shall be complied with.


e/ The order and procedures for licensing the manufacture of radio transmitters and/or receivers-transmitters:
- A dossier of application for permit shall consist of:
+ An application;
+ The enterprise�s organization and operation charter;
+ The production scheme with the following principal contents: category of equipment, technical properties (frequency, frequency band,
transmitting capacity of equipment�), technology and capacity of the production lines�


- Time limit for handling dossiers: The General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall evaluate and grant permits within
45 days after the receipt of valid dossiers. If there arise any matters which need to be re-examined, the above time-limit may be
extended but shall not exceed 60 days after receipt of valid dossiers. In case of refusal, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
shall send written reply to the enterprise within the above time-limit.
III. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE NO PERMIT
3.1 The conditional postal and telecommunication business lines which require no permit:


a/ Manufacture of post and telecommunication supplies and equipment (excluding radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters);
b/ Import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
c/ Purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agency;
e/ Agency for foreign express mail service companies;
f/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps.


3.2. Enterprises of all economic sectors that legally operate in Vietnam may register and do business in the domains specified at
Point 3.1 and shall be entitled to do business in such domains from the time they satisfy all business conditions set in this Circular
and commit themselves to maintain these conditions throughout the process of business operation.
3.3. During the process of business operation, enterprises must comply with law provisions on the goods and services quality, regulations
on information and advertisement, regulations on settlement of compensation claims as well as other relevant law provisions.


3.4. Business conditions for the manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification" issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before circulating them on the market.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


3.5. Business conditions for the import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before importing them.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.


b/ For foreign-made subscribed terminal devices which are imported for sale on the Vietnamese market, enterprises shall have to effect
the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


c/ For radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters, enterprises may import only those with a frequency or frequency band in line
with the planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations in Vietnam, issued together with the Prime Minister�s
Decision No. 85/1998/QD-TTg of April 16, 1998 approving Vietnam�s planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations
and other relevant regulations of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


d/ For fixed satellite transmitters, receiver-transmitters used in telecommunication operations and broadcasting operations, enterprises
shall have to request their customers wishing to use such equipment to apply for permits to use transmitters and radio frequencies,
issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications before carrying out import procedures;
e/ Enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and
Telecommunications General Department�s permits for use of radio transmitters and frequencies;


f/ The import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment for security and defense purposes shall comply with
the regulations of the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Defense.
3.6. Business conditions for the purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:


a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises may only deal in the purchase
and sale of supplies and equipment already certified for their standard conformity as prescribed;
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


c/ For the purchase and sale of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters, enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds
of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and Telecommunications General Department�s licenses for use
of radio transmitters and frequencies;
3.7. Conditions for acting as postal and telecommunication service provision agents:


a/ Enterprises wishing to act as postal and telecommunication service provision agents must sign agency contracts with postal and
telecommunication service-providing enterprises or telecommunication service-reselling enterprises (hereinafter called the principals
for short). The agency contracts must clearly state kinds of postal and telecommunication services the agents are permitted to provide,
the quality and charge of each kind of service and the commission rate enjoyed by the agents.


b/ Pledge is made to provide the right services with proper quality as stated in the agency contracts and to collect charges at the
rates applied by the principals to users.
c/ Places of postal and telecommunication service provision agents must be put up with the commercial names and logos of the principals;


d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agents must comply with the rules on postal and telecommunication services issued
by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications and submit to the inspection and supervision by the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications as well as competent State management bodies in the provision of postal and telecommunication services.
3.8. Conditions for acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies:


a/ Only enterprises licensed by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications to provide international postal services may
act as service agents (hereinafter called as agents for short) for foreign express mail service companies;
b/ Enterprises may sign agency contracts with foreign express mail service companies within the scope of international postal services
already licensed;
c/ Foreign express mail service companies that sign agency contracts must be those licensed to lawfully operate in one of the countries
with which Vietnam has established international post relations;


d/ Agency activities for foreign express mail service companies must ensure the national sovereignty and security as well as the interests
of service users and comply with the provisions of Vietnamese laws on post, tax, customs, information security and mail safety;


e/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies, on the basis of Vietnamese laws and agreements with foreign
express mail service companies, shall have to formulate framework agency contracts for uniform application within the whole enterprises
and register such model contracts with the General Department of Post and Telecommunications; print matters used in transactions
with service users must be expressed in Vietnamese and a foreign language.


f/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail companies shall have to announce and post up at the transaction places the
service charges, service quality norms and users� rights and obligations;
g/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies shall apply the annual regular or irregular regime of reporting
on the results of agency activities at the request of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.
3.9. Conditions for conducting business in the import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity
postage stamps:


a/ Only enterprises licensed to do business in mail service may conduct import and export of postage stamps, stamp publications and
commodity postage stamps;
b/ Enterprises that deal in the purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps must sign agency
contracts with mail service-providing enterprises;


c/ It is forbidden to purchase, sell, import or export any kind of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps,
which the General Department of Post and Telecommunications have suspended from issuance, banned from circulation or which have unhealthy
contents, incite or sow hatred among nations, infringe upon the national sovereignty and run counter to the Vietnamese traditional
practices and laws.
IV. IMPLEMENTATION PROVISIONS
4.1. This Circular takes effect 15 days after its signing. All the previous provisions which are contrary to this Circular are now
annulled.


4.2. Units of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall, within the scope of their relevant powers and tasks, have
to explain, guide, inspect and supervise the implementation of this Circular.
4.3. Enterprises shall have to strictly abide by the provisions of this Circular. Any problems arising in the course of implementation
should be promptly reported by enterprises to the General Department of Post and Telecommunications for guidance or explanation.

## 一、核心概括

经核查现有法规资料，**未检索到越南《招标法》（Law on Bidding）的任何条文**，因此无法就政府采购流程和投标人资质的具体规定给出基于法条的回答。以下仅就资料库中与“资质条件”“许可程序”相关的越南电信与互联网领域规定作参照性说明，并明确指出资料边界。


## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 资料库覆盖范围与《招标法》的缺失

**法规出处**：现有资料库包含越南《关于加强公共互联网代理点管理的指示》（07/2004/CT-BBCVT）【来源1】、《关于邮电与信息技术组织与运作的第75/2003/ND-CP号法令》【来源2】、《关于〈商法〉国际货物买卖活动实施细则的第12/2006/ND-CP号法令》【来源3】、《关于邮电与互联网领域有条件经营行业活动的第06/2000/TT-TCBD号通知》【来源4】以及《电信法》第63条【来源5】。

**深度解读**：上述法规均属邮电、电信、互联网及商事领域，**没有一部涉及政府采购招标程序或投标人资格审查**。越南《招标法》历经2005年首版及2013年、2023年多次修订，其核心内容包括招标方式（公开招标、限制招标、指定招标等）、投标人资格（财务能力、技术能力、经验业绩）、招标文件编制、评标标准与中标公示等，但这些内容在现有资料中完全空白。

**重点提示**：不得以电信领域的“许可条件”替代或类推《招标法》的“投标人资质”，二者法律性质不同——前者是行业准入行政许可，后者是采购程序中的竞争资格。

**实务指引**：如需准确回答该问题，应补充检索越南国会通过的《招标法》（Law No. 43/2013/QH13 及后续修订文本）及配套法令（如 Decree 63/2014/ND-CP）。在资料补齐前，不宜向客户出具确定性意见。

### 2. 参照：越南电信与互联网领域的“资质/许可”制度框架

**法规出处**：越南《第06/2000/TT-TCBD号通知》第2.1条、第2.2条、第2.3条【来源4】。

**深度解读**：该通知将邮电与互联网业务划分为“需许可证”与“无需许可证但须满足条件”两类。需许可证的业务包括建立国家电信骨干网、公共电信网并提供电信服务，建立互联网网络并提供IAP、ISP服务，建立邮政网络并提供邮政服务等；且从事这些业务的主体**必须是国有企业或国家持股占主导/特别股份的股份公司**。企业须先依法完成工商登记，再申请许可证，取得许可证后方可开业。

**重点提示**：这体现越南在关键基础设施领域对**所有制形式**设有准入限制，与一般政府采购中“投标人资质”评审逻辑不同，但可作为理解越南“资格条件”立法风格的参照。

**实务指引**：若中国企业拟进入越南电信或互联网上游业务，应首先核查自身所有制形式是否符合第2.2条要求，并预留许可证审批时间（部分许可审批时限为45至60天）。

### 3. 参照：代理与合同签订的前置登记要求

**法规出处**：越南《第07/2004/CT-BBCVT号指示》第一部分a项、b项【来源1】。

**深度解读**：该指示要求互联网服务提供商（ISP）和在线服务提供商（OSP）须告知并指导拟提供公共互联网服务的用户**先完成互联网代理业务登记**，之后方可签订代理合同；同时要求提供商制定统一的代理合同范本并报邮电部备案。合同内容除一般合同法规定外，还须加入代理业主张贴内部使用规定、登记线路号码、制止用户违规等责任条款。

**重点提示**：这反映越南监管的一个共性思路——**“先登记/许可、后签约履约”**，与招标程序中“先资格审查、后投标评标”在程序逻辑上有相似之处，但法律依据完全不同，不可混用。

**实务指引**：在越南开展代理类业务时，应将“工商登记—合同范本备案—签约—监督检查”作为标准合规流程，并保留登记凭证以备检查。

### 4. 资料不足的明确说明

**法规出处**：现有五个来源均未涉及《招标法》【来源1】【来源2】【来源3】【来源4】【来源5】。

**深度解读**：关于越南《招标法》对政府采购流程（招标方式选择、招标公告、投标文件递交与开标、评标委员会组成、中标决定与公示、异议与投诉）和投标人资质（独立法人资格、财务能力、技术能力、类似业绩、无腐败与失信记录等）的具体规定，**现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定**。知识图谱中出现的美国FAR条款（52.209-1、52.212-1）系美国联邦采购规则，与越南法无关，不能作为回答依据。

**重点提示**：跨境法律意见中，法域混淆是重大执业风险。美国FAR的“资格要求”条款与越南《招标法》的投标人资格审查在概念上相似，但适用法域、主管机关和法律后果截然不同。

**实务指引**：建议客户通过越南计划投资部或越南国家招标网（muasamcong.mpi.gov.vn）获取现行《招标法》及配套法令原文，或委托越南本地律师出具专项意见。


## 三、总结与建议

现有资料库**不含越南《招标法》条文**，故无法就政府采购流程与投标人资质给出有法条支撑的结论。资料中可参照的是越南电信互联网领域的许可与登记制度（第06/2000号通知、第07/2004号指示），其“先准入后经营”的逻辑可作背景理解，但不能替代《招标法》分析。

**行动指引**：一是补充检索越南《招标法》（43/2013/QH13及修订版）与Decree 63/2014/ND-CP等配套文本；二是区分“行业准入许可”与“采购投标资格”两个法律层面；三是涉及具体项目时，以越南国家招标网公告和招标文件（HSMT）为准。

**延伸提醒**：越南招标法规近年修订频繁，须确认文本时效性；中资企业参与越南政府采购还需关注《投资法》外资准入及本地化要求。

yearDIRECTIVE No. 07/2004/CT-BBCVT OF JULY 19, 2004 ON ENHANCING THE MANAGEMENT OF PUBLIC INTERNET AGENTS
Over the recent years, Vietnam's Internet has witnessed a fast development and exerted positive impacts on various aspects of the
national socio-economic life, thus actually bringing about great efficacies and creating favorable conditions for and effectively
supporting the implementation of the open-door and proactive international economic integration policies of the Party and the State.


Together with the general development of Internet, public Internet agents have also actively contributed to the universalization of
Internet services to people of all strata. However, besides positive aspects of this mode of service provision, many public Internet
access spots, which are providing Internet services in form of Internet service agents, have failed to comply with the law provisions
on Internet management, letting users arbitrarily access unhealthy information which may cause harms to the political security, social
order and safety and national cultural identity of Vietnam.


In order to enhance the management of activities of public Internet agents in strict compliance with the provisions of the Government's
Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP of August 23, 2001 on management, provision and use of Internet services, thus minimizing negative phenomena
which may occur in Internet agency activities, the Minister of Post and Telematics hereby instructs as follows:
Internet service providers (ISP) and telecommunications on-line service providers (OSP) shall:
a/ Notify and guide Internet service users who wish to provide public Internet services in making business registrations and signing


of agency contracts with Internet service providers. The signing of Internet agency contracts shall be effected only after the users
have registered the Internet agency business with the local business registries according to law provisions.
b/ Elaborate and promulgate the Regulation on management of Internet agents and model agency contracts for unified use by providers.
The providers' model Internet agency contracts must be sent to the Ministry of Post and Telematics. The contents of Internet agency
contracts, besides general law provisions on contracts, must be added with some points related to the responsibilities of agent owners,


more concretely as follows:
- Agent owners must post up internal regulations on the use of Internet services at their own establishments, which include the bans
prescribed in Article 11 of the Government's Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP of August 23, 2001 on management, provision and use of Internet
services.
- Agent owners must register their telephone numbers or serial numbers of their contracts on hiring of telecommunications transmission
lines used for Internet access with Internet service providers.
- Internet agent owners must guide service users in complying with the regulations on Internet use. When detecting service users who


intentionally violate the regulations on Internet use or violate internal regulations on Internet service use, Internet agents shall
have to immediately stop the service users' violations.
- The agent owners' acts of facilitating or intentionally covering up acts of stealing passwords or access accounts; spreading viruses;
accessing electronic news pages or propagating or spreading documents with depraved or obscene contents, violating the fine customs
and traditions or infringing upon the national security, shall constitute grounds for providers to stop providing services and suspend
the agency contracts.


c/ Work out plans on, and take the initiative in conducting, the inspection and supervision of the performance of the signed contracts
by the Internet agents. In the course of inspection and supervision of the performance of agency contracts, if providers have enough
grounds to conclude that agent owners' violations of contract provisions constitute the conditions for suspending contracts, they
shall make written records thereon, stop providing services and concurrently send written notices on law violations by such agents
to the local Post and Telematics Departments or Services.


d/ Review the management of Internet agents by providers according to the contents of the Government's Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP, the
guiding documents of the Ministry of Post and Telematics, the Ministry of Culture and Information and the Ministry of Public Security
as well as the provisions of this Directive, paying special attention to the agent management regulation; contents of agency contracts;
plans on supervision and inspection of contract performance by agents. Where they deem the agent management is not up to the set


requirements, providers shall have to temporarily suspend the signing of new Internet agency contracts for reorganizing their management
work and reporting such to the Ministry of Post and Telematics.
Telecommunications enterprises shall have to coordinate with Internet service providers in disconnecting Internet agents' telephone
numbers or telecommunications transmission lines for Internet access if they receive written notices of the Inspectorate of the Ministry
of Post and Telematics or the local Post and Telematics Departments or Services on law violations committed by agents and their requests


for disconnecting telephone numbers or telecommunications transmission lines for Internet access.
The Post and Telematics Ministry's Inspectorate shall expeditiously assume the prime responsibility for elaborating a joint circular
guiding Article 41 of the Government's Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP of August 23, 2001 on Internet service management, provision and
use regarding violation acts, forms and levels of sanction against administrative violations in Internet domain. The Inspectorate
of the Ministry of Post and Telematics, the provincial/municipal Post and Telematics Departments and Services shall:


a/ Work out plans on, and conduct, inspection or examination of Internet service providers in the management of public Internet agents.
In the course of inspection or examination, if detecting that providers fail to meet the requirements of the agent management according
to regulations, the Inspectorate of the Ministry of Post and Telematics shall request in writing those providers to temporarily suspend
the signing of new agency contracts for reorganizing their agent management.
b/ Take initiative in coordinating with the local administrations and the concerned ministries and branches in organizing the inspection


of activities of public Internet agents, especially those in large cities like Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh city, Da Nang, Hai Phong, Can Tho,
etc.
c/ Resolutely sanction administrative violations committed by service providers and public Internet agents regarding law provisions
on Internet according to their respective State management competence and functions prescribed in the Ordinance on Handling of Administrative
Violations, the Government's Decree No. 142/2004/ND-CP and Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP.
The Telecommunications Department shall coordinate with the concerned units under the Ministry of Culture and Information and the


Ministry of Public Security in studying and organizing the elaboration of a joint circular on management of public Internet agents
for promulgation in 2004.
The Minister of Post and Telematics shall request Internet service providers, telecommunications enterprises and concerned units to
strictly implement this Directive.
Minister of Post and Telematics
DO TRUNG TA

THE GENERAL DEPARTMENT OF POST AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
CIRCULAR No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD OF SEPTEMBER 29, 2000 GUIDING THE ACTIVITIES REGARDING THE CONDITIONAL BUSINESS LINES IN THE DOMAINS
OF POST, TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND INTERNET

In furtherance of the provisions of Decree No. 03/2000/ND-CP of February 3, 2000 guiding the implementation of a number of articles
of the Enterprises Law and Decree No. 30/2000/ND-CP of August 11, 2000 on the cancellation of a number of permits and licenses and
the conversion of a number of licenses into business conditions and, at the same time, in order to create favorable conditions for
activities of enterprises; after consulting with several concerned ministries and branches, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
hereby guides a number of contents of business activities in the domains of post, telecommunications and internet as follows:
I. GENERAL PROVISIONS


1.1 This Circular provides guidance for enterprises engaged in business activities in the domain of post and telecommunications and
Internet, as prescribed by law, which fall under the conditional business lines.
1.2 Post and/or telecommunications enterprises are enterprises engaged in business activities in one or several domains prescribed
in the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on post and telecommunications. The conditional post and telecommunication
business lines include:
a/ Provision of postal and telecommunication services;
b/ Manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;


c/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Printing of postage stamps; production, import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage
stamps.
1.3 Internet services-providing enterprises are enterprises dealing in Internet services specified in the Government�s Decree No.
21/CP of March 5, 1997 issuing the Provisional Regulation on the management, establishment and use of the Internet in Vietnam".
The conditional Internet business lines include:
a/ Provision of Internet access services (IAP);
b/ Provision of Internet services (ISP).


1.4 The postal, telecommunication and Internet domains fall under the conditional business lines, where some business domains require
permits of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications while some others do not but must satisfy the conditions set in
this Circular.
1.5 Various kinds of permits and certificates used for technical and professional management prescribed in Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP
in order to ensure the network and service quality, ensure safety for operation of public and exclusive postal and telecommunication
networks and ensure the interests of users shall not be regulated by this Circular.


II. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE PERMITS
2.1 The post, telecommunication and Internet business lines that require permits include:
a/ Establishment of national telecommunication backbone networks, public telecommunication networks and provision (direct or for resale)
of telecommunication services (basic, value-added);
b/ Establishment of Internet networks and provision of Internet services (IAP and ISP);
c/ Establishment of postal networks and provision of postal services;
d/ Printing of postage stamps;
e/ Manufacture of radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters.


2.2. Enterprises conducting business activities in the domains specified at Points a, b, c and d, Section 2.1 shall be State enterprises
or joint-stock companies where the State holds the predominant or special shares. For the domain specified at Point e, Section 2.1,
the business subjects shall be enterprises of any economic sector. Enterprises may do business in these domains under conditions
and according to the operating duration specified in their permits and start their business activities only when they obtain their
licenses.


2.3. Enterprises must make business registration according to law provisions before carrying out procedures applying for permits to
do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above.
2.4. The conditions, order and procedures for granting of permits to do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above shall
be as follows:
a/ For permits stated at Point a , the provisions in Circular No. 04/1998/TT-TCBD of September 29, 1998 of the General Department
of Post and Telecommunications guiding the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on telecommunication networks
and services, shall be complied with.


b/ For permits specified at Point b, the provisions of Joint Circular No. 08/TTLT of May 24, 197 of the General Department of Post
and Telecommunications, the Ministry of the Interior (now the Ministry of Public Security) and the Ministry of Culture and Information
guiding the licensing of the connection, provision and use of Internet in Vietnam, shall be complied with;


c/ For permits specified at Point c, the provisions of Circular No. 02/1998/TT-TCBD of June 20, 1998 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications guiding the implementation of the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP on postal networks and services,
shall be complied with;
d/ For permits specified at Point d, the provisions of Decision No. 217/2000/QD-TCBD of March 6, 2000 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications issuing the Regulation on the professional management of postage stamps, shall be complied with.


e/ The order and procedures for licensing the manufacture of radio transmitters and/or receivers-transmitters:
- A dossier of application for permit shall consist of:
+ An application;
+ The enterprise�s organization and operation charter;
+ The production scheme with the following principal contents: category of equipment, technical properties (frequency, frequency band,
transmitting capacity of equipment�), technology and capacity of the production lines�


- Time limit for handling dossiers: The General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall evaluate and grant permits within
45 days after the receipt of valid dossiers. If there arise any matters which need to be re-examined, the above time-limit may be
extended but shall not exceed 60 days after receipt of valid dossiers. In case of refusal, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
shall send written reply to the enterprise within the above time-limit.
III. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE NO PERMIT
3.1 The conditional postal and telecommunication business lines which require no permit:


a/ Manufacture of post and telecommunication supplies and equipment (excluding radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters);
b/ Import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
c/ Purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agency;
e/ Agency for foreign express mail service companies;
f/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps.


3.2. Enterprises of all economic sectors that legally operate in Vietnam may register and do business in the domains specified at
Point 3.1 and shall be entitled to do business in such domains from the time they satisfy all business conditions set in this Circular
and commit themselves to maintain these conditions throughout the process of business operation.
3.3. During the process of business operation, enterprises must comply with law provisions on the goods and services quality, regulations
on information and advertisement, regulations on settlement of compensation claims as well as other relevant law provisions.


3.4. Business conditions for the manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification" issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before circulating them on the market.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


3.5. Business conditions for the import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before importing them.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.


b/ For foreign-made subscribed terminal devices which are imported for sale on the Vietnamese market, enterprises shall have to effect
the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


c/ For radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters, enterprises may import only those with a frequency or frequency band in line
with the planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations in Vietnam, issued together with the Prime Minister�s
Decision No. 85/1998/QD-TTg of April 16, 1998 approving Vietnam�s planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations
and other relevant regulations of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


d/ For fixed satellite transmitters, receiver-transmitters used in telecommunication operations and broadcasting operations, enterprises
shall have to request their customers wishing to use such equipment to apply for permits to use transmitters and radio frequencies,
issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications before carrying out import procedures;
e/ Enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and
Telecommunications General Department�s permits for use of radio transmitters and frequencies;


f/ The import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment for security and defense purposes shall comply with
the regulations of the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Defense.
3.6. Business conditions for the purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:


a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises may only deal in the purchase
and sale of supplies and equipment already certified for their standard conformity as prescribed;
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


c/ For the purchase and sale of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters, enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds
of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and Telecommunications General Department�s licenses for use
of radio transmitters and frequencies;
3.7. Conditions for acting as postal and telecommunication service provision agents:


a/ Enterprises wishing to act as postal and telecommunication service provision agents must sign agency contracts with postal and
telecommunication service-providing enterprises or telecommunication service-reselling enterprises (hereinafter called the principals
for short). The agency contracts must clearly state kinds of postal and telecommunication services the agents are permitted to provide,
the quality and charge of each kind of service and the commission rate enjoyed by the agents.


b/ Pledge is made to provide the right services with proper quality as stated in the agency contracts and to collect charges at the
rates applied by the principals to users.
c/ Places of postal and telecommunication service provision agents must be put up with the commercial names and logos of the principals;


d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agents must comply with the rules on postal and telecommunication services issued
by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications and submit to the inspection and supervision by the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications as well as competent State management bodies in the provision of postal and telecommunication services.
3.8. Conditions for acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies:


a/ Only enterprises licensed by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications to provide international postal services may
act as service agents (hereinafter called as agents for short) for foreign express mail service companies;
b/ Enterprises may sign agency contracts with foreign express mail service companies within the scope of international postal services
already licensed;
c/ Foreign express mail service companies that sign agency contracts must be those licensed to lawfully operate in one of the countries
with which Vietnam has established international post relations;


d/ Agency activities for foreign express mail service companies must ensure the national sovereignty and security as well as the interests
of service users and comply with the provisions of Vietnamese laws on post, tax, customs, information security and mail safety;


e/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies, on the basis of Vietnamese laws and agreements with foreign
express mail service companies, shall have to formulate framework agency contracts for uniform application within the whole enterprises
and register such model contracts with the General Department of Post and Telecommunications; print matters used in transactions
with service users must be expressed in Vietnamese and a foreign language.


f/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail companies shall have to announce and post up at the transaction places the
service charges, service quality norms and users� rights and obligations;
g/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies shall apply the annual regular or irregular regime of reporting
on the results of agency activities at the request of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.
3.9. Conditions for conducting business in the import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity
postage stamps:


a/ Only enterprises licensed to do business in mail service may conduct import and export of postage stamps, stamp publications and
commodity postage stamps;
b/ Enterprises that deal in the purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps must sign agency
contracts with mail service-providing enterprises;


c/ It is forbidden to purchase, sell, import or export any kind of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps,
which the General Department of Post and Telecommunications have suspended from issuance, banned from circulation or which have unhealthy
contents, incite or sow hatred among nations, infringe upon the national sovereignty and run counter to the Vietnamese traditional
practices and laws.
IV. IMPLEMENTATION PROVISIONS
4.1. This Circular takes effect 15 days after its signing. All the previous provisions which are contrary to this Circular are now
annulled.


4.2. Units of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall, within the scope of their relevant powers and tasks, have
to explain, guide, inspect and supervise the implementation of this Circular.
4.3. Enterprises shall have to strictly abide by the provisions of this Circular. Any problems arising in the course of implementation
should be promptly reported by enterprises to the General Department of Post and Telecommunications for guidance or explanation.
General Director of Post and Telecommunications
MAI LIEM TRUC

## 一、核心概括

越南对数字签名认证服务机构实行**分类许可与登记管理**：提供公共数字签名认证服务须经许可（Article 8），提供专用数字签名认证服务须办理登记（Article 4），向机构颁发数字证书须遵循法定程序（Article 10）。核心规范为第37/2009/TT-BTTTT号通知，配套第26/2007/ND-CP号法令。

## 二、法律依据详解

**要点一：公共数字签名认证服务的许可制度**

1. 法规出处：越南《关于数字签名认证服务机构许可、登记与认可档案及程序的規定》（第37/2009/TT-BTTTT号通知）第8条【来源2】。
2. 深度解读：该条确立"公共数字签名认证服务"的**事前许可制**。所谓"公共"服务，指面向社会不特定主体提供数字证书签发与认证，具有准公共信用基础设施属性，故立法采许可制而非登记制，以事前审查申请人的技术能力、安全保障与合规条件。这与专用服务（仅面向内部或特定群体）的登记制形成梯度监管：风险外溢程度越高，准入管制越严。
3. 重点提示：未取得许可擅自提供公共服务，属无证经营，可能面临行政处罚及服务无效风险；许可申请档案与程序须严格依照该通知要求准备，材料不齐将导致受理延迟。
4. 实务指引：拟进入越南公共认证市场的机构，应首先对照第8条梳理申请档案清单，重点准备技术方案、安全评估与人员资质材料；建议在正式提交前与主管机关进行预沟通，明确审查口径，避免反复补正。

**要点二：专用数字签名认证服务的登记制度**

1. 法规出处：同通知第4条【来源1】。
2. 深度解读：专用认证服务（如企业内部、行业封闭场景）采**登记制**，监管强度低于许可制。立法意图在于：专用服务影响范围有限，以登记备案替代实质审批，降低市场准入门槛，同时保留主管机关事后监督的抓手。登记并非"无监管"，而是将监管重心从"事前准入"后移至"事中事后合规"。
3. 重点提示：登记义务的触发时点是"开展运营"之前，先运营后登记构成程序违法；登记信息发生变更时应及时更新，否则可能影响服务效力的对外证明。
4. 实务指引：企业开展专用认证业务前，应完成登记并留存登记凭证；建立内部合规台账，记录服务对象范围，确保"专用"属性不被突破——一旦实际面向公众提供服务，即可能被认定为应取得许可而构成违规。

**要点三：向机构颁发数字证书的程序**

1. 法规出处：同通知第10条【来源4】；配套申请材料依第26/2007/ND-CP号法令第21条及通知第2条【来源5】。
2. 深度解读：第10条规定向公共认证服务机构颁发数字证书的程序，申请材料包括**按附录V格式填写的数字证书申请表**，以及根认证机构（Root CA）在官网公布的认证规则所要求的文件【来源5】。这表明越南采用"申请表+认证规则动态指引"的双层材料结构：法定表格固定基础信息，认证规则承载技术与安全要求并可动态更新，兼顾确定性与灵活性。
3. 重点提示：认证规则发布于根认证机构网站，申请人须以提交时的最新版本为准，援引过时规则将导致材料不符；申请表须严格使用附录V规定格式。
4. 实务指引：提交前逐项核对附录V表格与Root CA网站现行认证规则清单，形成材料对照表；保留网站规则版本截图作为提交时点的证据，防范后续争议。

**要点四：数字签名使用的内部规范衔接**

1. 法规出处：越南《贸易部数字签名使用规程》（第25/2006/QD-BTM号决定）第三章总则部分【来源3】。
2. 深度解读：该决定针对贸易部内部数字签名的使用作出规定，明确办公厅、电子商务局负责人及贸易部干部公务员的实施义务【来源3】。其意义在于：认证服务机构的合规不仅受专门通知约束，使用端（政府机关）的内部规程亦构成生态闭环——认证机构签发的证书须能在使用端被正确采纳，机构应关注主要客户所在行业的签名使用规范。
3. 重点提示：该决定为部门内部规程，不直接设定认证机构的义务，但影响证书的互操作与采纳标准。
4. 实务指引：认证机构在服务政府客户时，应核查对方适用的内部数字签名规程，确保证书类型、算法与格式满足其要求，降低"签发了但用不了"的落地风险。

## 三、总结与建议

越南对数字签名认证服务机构采**分级监管**：公共服务须依第37/2009/TT-BTTTT号通知第8条取得许可，专用服务依第4条办理登记，颁发证书依第10条及第26/2007/ND-CP号法令第21条提交申请【来源1】【来源2】【来源4】【来源5】。行动上，先定性服务类型，再对应准备许可或登记材料，并动态跟踪Root CA认证规则。

延伸提醒：其一，服务性质可能随业务扩张从"专用"变为"公共"，须及时升级为许可；其二，关注电子签名法政策层面（如签名设备多样化、互操作性）对认证业务的长期影响；其三，具体许可时限与审查标准，现有资料未完整呈现，建议以主管机关最新指引为准。

## 一、核心概括

亚洲各法域个人资料保护立法呈现"原则导向"与"分散立法"两条路径。马来西亚Act 709确立七项核心原则并设数据主体查阅更正权；新加坡PDPA 2012以统一定义体系覆盖公私机构；澳门则依托第8/2005号《个人资料保护法》作为基础法，在专项立法中援引适用。三地共同点是均承认数据主体权利与合法处理要求，差异在于立法集中度、适用范围广度及执行机制。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 马来西亚：七项原则构成的集中式保护框架

**法规出处**：马来西亚《Personal Data Protection Act 2010》（Act 709）第5条确立个人资料保护原则体系，涵盖一般原则、通知与选择原则、披露原则、安全原则、保留原则、数据完整性原则及查阅原则【来源1】。

**深度解读**：Act 709采取"原则立法"模式，将实体义务浓缩为七项原则，适用于商业交易中的个人资料处理。第5条本身是原则清单的索引性条款，各原则的具体义务需结合后续条文理解。立法意图在于以统一原则覆盖资料处理的完整生命周期——从收集（通知与选择）、持有（安全与保留）、使用（披露限制）到资料主体权利（查阅与更正）。值得注意的是，知识图谱显示第12条赋予资料主体查阅权及更正不准确、不完整、误导性或过时资料的权利，且该权利仅在法定拒绝情形下受限【知识图谱关联】。

**重点提示**：七项原则并非并列孤立，而是相互衔接的义务链条。例如通知与选择原则要求收集前告知目的，直接影响后续披露原则的合规判断。资料主体依第42条还可发出书面通知，要求数据使用者停止或不得开始特定目的的处理【知识图谱关联】——这是超越查阅更正权的"处理反对权"，实务中常被忽视。

**实务指引**：企业应建立"原则对照清单"，逐项核验收集通知、目的限定、安全措施、保留期限、查阅响应流程是否落地。常见误区是将七项原则视为一次性合规审查，而忽略其持续性义务属性——保留原则和安全原则要求动态维护，而非收集时点的一次性动作。

### 2. 新加坡：以定义体系为基石的统一立法

**法规出处**：新加坡《Personal Data Protection Act 2012》第2条集中界定"个人资料""组织""处理""资料中介"等核心概念【来源3】。

**深度解读**：新加坡PDPA第2条的定义体系具有三个显著特征。其一，"个人资料"采"可识别性"标准——无论资料是否真实，只要能从该资料或该资料与组织可获取的其他信息中识别个人，即属个人资料【来源3】。其二，"组织"定义极具域外延展性，明确包括不在新加坡注册、不在新加坡居住或营业的个体、公司、社团【来源3】，这意味着境外主体处理新加坡境内个人资料亦可能受辖。其三，"处理"定义涵盖记录、持有、组织、改编、检索、组合、传输、擦除或销毁等全链条操作【来源3】，与马来西亚的"处理"概念功能相当但表述更细。

**重点提示**：第2条还区分了"资料中介"（代他组织处理资料者，不含该组织雇员）与资料使用者，这一区分影响责任分配。"商业联系方式"被单独定义，暗示其在特定场景下可能适用不同规则。此外"公开可获取"资料的定义限定了公开来源的边界，企业不得随意以"已公开"为由规避义务。

**实务指引**：跨国企业应首先以第2条定义做"管辖触发测试"——是否存在处理新加坡个人资料的组织（含境外主体）。其次，梳理自身在资料链条中的角色（使用者还是中介），据此分配合规责任。建议将定义条款转化为内部数据分类标准，尤其注意"衍生个人资料"与"用户活动数据"的独立定义，避免遗漏合规范围。

### 3. 澳门：基础法加专项援引的分散模式

**法规出处**：澳门第8/2005号法律《个人资料保护法》为一般性基础法；第7/2017号法律《非强制性中央公积金制度》及第20/2020号法律《会计师专业及执业资格制度》均设专条援引该法，允许社会保障基金、委员会等机构以包括资料互联在内的方式与其他公共实体提供、互换、确认及使用利害关系人个人资料【来源2】【来源4】。

**深度解读**：澳门的立法路径与马来西亚、新加坡显著不同——不制定统一的个人资料保护单行法典，而以第8/2005号法律为底座，在各部门法中"点状援引"。第7/2017号法律第5条和第20/2020号法律第103条的表述几乎一致，均以"可根据第8/2005号法律的规定"作为合法性前提，再授权特定公共实体间的资料互联【来源2】【来源4】。这种"授权+援引"结构表明：专项立法本身不创设新的资料保护标准，而是将第8/2005号法律的合规要求嵌入行政程序。

**重点提示**：第2/2020号法律《电子政务》第17条进一步明确，公共部门执行个人资料操作（包括比较和互联）须"尊重自然人的权利或受法律保护的利益，并按第8/2005号法律的规定进行"【来源5】。这揭示澳门模式的核心风险点：资料互联的合法性不来自专项授权本身，而取决于是否符合第8/2005号法律的原则与条件。专项授权仅解决"能不能互联"，基础法解决"互联是否合规"。

**实务指引**：在澳门运营的机构（尤其是参与公共基金、专业资格管理的实体）应建立"双层合规审查"：第一层核查专项立法是否授权特定资料处理或互联；第二层回归第8/2005号法律，评估处理目的正当性、资料适当性及当事人权利保障。常见误区是仅凭专项法条即认为资料互联当然合法，忽略基础法的实质约束。

### 4. 三法域框架的结构性差异

**法规出处**：综合马来西亚Act 709第5条【来源1】、新加坡PDPA第2条【来源3】及澳门第8/2005号法律与专项立法的援引结构【来源2】【来源4】【来源5】。

**深度解读**：三地差异可从三个维度把握。**立法集中度**：马来西亚、新加坡采统一单行法，澳门采基础法加分散援引。**适用范围**：新加坡"组织"定义明确延及境外主体，马来西亚以"商业交易"为适用锚点，澳门则通过各部门法界定适用主体，覆盖面取决于专项立法密度。**权利配置**：马来西亚明确列举查阅权、更正权及第42条的处理反对权；新加坡以定义体系支撑后续义务条款；澳门则将权利保障回归第8/2005号法律统一处理。

**重点提示**：框架差异直接影响合规策略的可移植性。在马来西亚有效的"七原则清单"不能直接套用于澳门，因后者需逐项核查专项授权与基础法的双重合规。新加坡的域外管辖定义则要求境外企业优先做管辖识别。

**实务指引**：跨境运营企业宜制作"法域合规矩阵"，按立法模式、适用触发条件、资料主体权利类型、资料互联规则四列对照三地要求，避免以单一法域模板覆盖全区域。

## 三、总结与建议

| 对比维度 | 马来西亚 Act 709 | 新加坡 PDPA 2012 | 澳门第8/2005号法律体系 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 立法模式 | 统一单行法，七项原则 | 统一单行法，定义先行 | 基础法+专项援引 |
| 适用锚点 | 商业交易中的资料处理 | 组织（含境外主体）处理资料 | 依专项立法界定主体 |
| 资料主体权利 | 查阅、更正、处理反对权 | 由定义体系支撑后续条款 | 回归基础法统一保障 |
| 资料互联 | 受披露原则约束 | 受同意及目的限制约束 | 须专项授权+基础法双重合规 |
| 严格程度 | 中等，原则导向 | 较高，域外延展 | 分散，依赖专项立法密度 |

三地共同承认资料主体权利与合法处理要求，核心差异在于立法集中度与适用触发机制。**行动指引**：企业进入任一法域前，先做管辖触发测试，再按该法域的框架逻辑（原则清单/定义体系/双层审查）搭建合规流程。**延伸提醒**：其一，马来西亚第42条的处理反对权常被遗漏，应纳入权利响应机制；其二，新加坡"组织"定义的域外效力意味着境外总部亦可能被追责；其三，澳门模式下不可仅凭专项法条主张资料互联合法，须回溯第8/2005号法律的实质要求。

## 一、核心概括

关于亚太各国在FATF反洗钱合规标准执行上的整体表现，现有法规资料暂未提供直接涵盖亚太地区FATF互评估结果的明确规定或评估报告。资料库中仅包含美国财政部FinCEN依据《银行保密法》对货币基金、银行、贷款金融公司、贵金属交易商及信用卡系统运营商等五类金融机构的反洗钱项目要求，可作为理解FATF标准在美国落地执行的参照，但无法据此推断亚太各国的合规表现。


## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 资料库的覆盖范围与局限

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Mutual Funds》1024.210【来源1】、《Rules for Banks (BSAAML)》1020.210【来源2】、《Rules for Real Estate》1029.210【来源3】、《Rules for Casinos and Card Clubs》1027.210【来源4】、《Rules for Dealers in Precious Metals》1028.210【来源5】。

**深度解读**：上述五个来源均为美国联邦法规（31 CFR Chapter X），分别针对共同基金、银行、贷款或金融公司、贵金属/宝石/珠宝交易商、信用卡系统运营商设定反洗钱项目的最低要求。这些条文体现的是FATF建议在美国国内法中的转化实施，而非对亚太各国执行情况的评估。FATF互评估（Mutual Evaluation）结果通常发布为各司法管辖区的相互评估报告（MER）及后续跟进报告，属于FATF官方公开文件，并非美国CFR法规的内容。

**重点提示**：不能将美国法规的严格程度等同于亚太各国的执行水平；各法域对FATF建议的转化方式、监管强度、执法力度存在显著差异，需以FATF互评估报告及亚太反洗钱组织（APG）的评估文件为准。

**实务指引**：如需评估某一亚太法域的合规表现，应查阅FATF官网公布的该法域互评估报告及后续跟进报告，重点关注技术合规性（TC）与有效性（EO）两项评级；同时参考APG发布的区域评估摘要。企业开展跨境业务尽职调查时，可将FATF“黑名单/灰名单”及APG评估结论作为风险分级依据。

### 2. 美国反洗钱项目的核心要素——可作为比较基准

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Banks (BSAAML)》1020.210(b)(2)【来源2】；《Rules for Mutual Funds》1024.210(b)【来源1】。

**深度解读**：两部法规均要求反洗钱项目至少包含五项核心要素：**内部控制体系**、**独立测试**、**合规负责人指定**、**持续培训**、**基于风险的客户尽职调查**（含理解客户关系性质与目的、持续监测可疑交易、维护更新客户信息，并将法人客户受益所有人信息纳入客户信息范围）。这一“五要素”结构与FATF建议第10条（客户尽职调查）、第18条（内部控制与合规）高度对应，是评估任何法域反洗钱制度是否“技术合规”的基本标尺。

**重点提示**：受益所有人识别（beneficial ownership）是FATF 2012年建议修订后的重点，美国于2016年通过1024.210(b)(5)(ii)和1020.210(b)(2)(v)(B)将其纳入；亚太各法域对受益所有人门槛（如25%持股）和登记机制的落实程度不一，是互评估中常见的扣分项。

**实务指引**：企业可比照“五要素”框架自查各亚太分支机构的合规项目完整性；重点关注受益所有人信息的采集与更新机制是否达到FATF建议第24条、第25条的要求。

### 3. 风险为本方法在不同行业的差异化落地

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Casinos and Card Clubs》1027.210(b)(1)【来源4】；《Rules for Real Estate》1029.210(b)(1)【来源3】。

**深度解读**：贵金属交易商条文要求基于产品类型、客户与供应商性质、分销渠道、地理区位等因素开展风险评估，并列举了异常支付方式、客户不愿提供完整信息、要求不留正常业务记录等可疑交易指示因素【来源4】。贷款金融公司条文则要求将代理商和经纪人纳入反洗钱项目，并获取有效项目所需的全部客户相关信息【来源3】。这体现了FATF“风险为本方法”（RBA）在不同行业的具体化——高风险行业（如贵金属现金交易）适用更细化的可疑指标，中介渠道较多的行业（如贷款金融）强调渠道整合。

**重点提示**：风险为本不等于降低标准，而是要求风险评估有书面依据、可被监管验证。独立测试的范围和频率应与风险评估相称【来源4】【来源3】。

**实务指引**：在亚太多法域运营的集团，应建立统一的集团层面风险评估框架，同时允许各法域根据本地FATF互评估结论和监管指引调整行业风险参数；保留风险评估文档以备监管检查。

### 4. 合规负责人与独立测试的制度刚性

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Dealers in Precious Metals》1028.210(b)(2)、(b)(4)【来源5】；《Rules for Banks (BSAAML)》1020.210(b)(2)(ii)-(iii)【来源2】。

**深度解读**：各条文均要求指定合规负责人并保证独立测试由非项目运营人员执行——贵金属交易商条文明确测试人不得是合规负责人或参与项目运营的人员【来源5】；银行条文允许由银行内部人员或外部方进行独立测试【来源2】。这一“职能分离”设计旨在防止自我监督失效，是FATF建议第18条内部控制要求的具体体现。

**重点提示**：独立测试的“独立性”是监管检查的高频问询点；内部人员测试时须确保其不承担项目日常运营职责，否则可能被认定为测试无效。

**实务指引**：建议在亚太各实体层面明确合规负责人的任命文件与职责清单，独立测试报告应留存备查，测试范围与频率的确定依据应形成书面记录。

### 5. 董事会/高级管理层审批与监管可及性

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Mutual Funds》1024.210(a)【来源1】；《Rules for Banks (BSAAML)》1020.210(b)(3)【来源2】；《Rules for Real Estate》1029.210(a)【来源3】。

**深度解读**：共同基金项目须经董事会或受托人书面批准，并可供SEC检查【来源1】；无联邦功能监管者的银行须由董事会或同等治理机构批准，并应FinCEN要求提供项目副本【来源2】；贷款金融公司项目须经高级管理层批准【来源3】。这体现了FATF建议第18条关于“高级管理层应确保建立合规制度”的治理要求——治理层审批是项目合法性的形式要件，也是监管问责的抓手。

**重点提示**：审批形式（书面决议、会议纪要）和监管可及性（随时可提供副本）是程序性合规要点，实务中常因文档缺失被认定为违规。

**实务指引**：在亚太各法域设立子公司或分支时，应将反洗钱项目提交当地治理机构审批并形成书面记录；建立监管问询响应机制，确保项目文件可在合理时限内提供。


## 三、总结与建议

**现有法规资料无法回答亚太各国FATF合规表现这一具体问题**——资料库仅含美国31 CFR Chapter X下五类金融机构的反洗钱项目要求，属于美国国内法对FATF建议的转化，不构成对亚太法域的评估。可提炼的通用要点是：FATF标准落地的核心检验维度包括“五要素”项目结构、风险为本方法、受益所有人识别、合规负责人与独立测试的职能分离、治理层审批与监管可及性。

**行动指引**：评估亚太各国表现，应以FATF官网互评估报告及APG评估文件为第一手依据，重点关注技术合规性与有效性评级、后续跟进进展。

**延伸提醒**：其一，FATF“灰名单”法域在跨境业务中通常触发强化尽职调查，需动态跟踪；其二，各法域对受益所有人门槛和登记机制差异较大，集团合规政策应保留本地化调整空间；其三，美国条文中的独立测试、风险评估文档化等要求可作为内部对标基准，但不得直接推定为亚太各国的法定标准。

## 一、核心概括

韩国《电子签名法》明确确立**技术中立**原则：电子签名不因电子形式而被否定法律效力，在法定或约定情形下与手写签名、签名盖章具有同等效力（第3条）。该法同时通过类型化定义（电子签名、认证、证书、认证服务提供者等）构建效力认定基础，并以政府政策义务保障安全性与可靠性。不同法域在效力认定上多采功能等同原则，但在类型划分（如是否区分高级/合格签名）上存在差异。以下基于韩国法展开分析。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 效力认定的基本原则：不得仅因电子形式而否定

**法规出处**：韩国《ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE ACT》第3条【来源4】。

**深度解读**：该条第1款规定，电子签名不得**仅因**其采用电子形式而被否认作为手写签名、签名盖章或记名盖章的法律效力。这确立了“功能等同”的底层逻辑——法律评价的重心在于签名能否实现身份识别与签署事实确认的功能，而非载体形式。第2款进一步规定，当依据法令或当事人协议选择电子签名作为签名方式时，电子签名与手写签名具有**同等效力**。立法意图在于消除电子商务与电子政务中的形式障碍，与第1条“确保电子文件的安全可靠、促进电子签名使用”的立法目的相呼应【来源5】。

**重点提示**：第1款的“不得仅因形式否定”是消极保护，不等于任何电子签名在任何场景下自动等同于手写签名；第2款的“同等效力”以“依法令或协议选定”为前提，属于积极赋权。两者层次不同，实务中不可混用。

**实务指引**：企业在合同中应明确约定采用电子签名及具体技术方案；在法定要求签名、盖章的场景，需先确认该法域是否已通过立法承认电子签名可替代书面形式，并保留签署过程的身份验证与时间戳证据。

### 2. 类型划分的基础：以定义条款构建的签名与认证体系

**法规出处**：韩国《ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE ACT》第2条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：该条以定义方式完成类型划分：**电子文件**（电子形式生成、传输、接收或存储的数据）、**电子签名**（附着于或逻辑关联于电子文件、用于识别签名人并验证签署事实的电子数据）、**电子签名生成数据**（签名人用于生成签名的电子数据）、**电子签名生成设备**（实施签名的电子手段）、**电子签名认证**（验证并证明生成数据与订阅者唯一关联的行为）、**证书**、**认证服务提供者**、**订阅者**与**使用者**。这一体系的特点是：法律并未按“简单/高级/合格”分级赋予不同效力，而是以“认证”为核心构建可信基础设施，通过认证服务间接支撑签名的可靠性评价。

**重点提示**：定义条款本身不直接创设效力差异，但“认证”与“证书”的存在意味着经认证的签名在举证与可靠性推定上更具优势。注意“订阅者”与“使用者”是不同主体，权利义务配置不同。

**实务指引**：跨境交易中应核查对方签名是否由持牌认证服务提供者签发证书，并保存证书链与认证记录；企业内部应区分“签名人生成数据”的保管责任与“使用者”的验证责任，避免混同。

### 3. 可靠性保障：政府政策义务与安全加密要求

**法规出处**：韩国《ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE ACT》第4条【来源2】。

**深度解读**：该条课以政府制定并实施电子签名发展政策的义务，涵盖提升可靠性、生成设备多样化、促进使用、改进签名方案与修订相关法规、保护订阅者与使用者权益、促进**互操作性**、技术开发与标准化、人才培养、使用**安全加密**确保可靠性、包括外国电子签名**互认**在内的国际合作、公共服务用电子签名的安全管理等。立法意图在于通过公共政策供给弥补技术中立原则可能带来的可靠性参差，使“形式中立”不至于滑向“可靠性虚无”。

**重点提示**：政策义务条款不直接赋予私人诉权，但构成监管框架与标准制定的依据；其中“互操作性”与“国际互认”对跨境电子签名效力承认具有指引意义，但互认的具体安排仍需依据双边或多边协议及对方法域规定判断。

**实务指引**：涉及公共服务或跨境业务的企业，应关注韩国政府依第4条发布的技术标准与互认进展；在争议中可将是否符合安全加密与标准化要求作为证明签名可靠性的辅助论据。

### 4. 时间确认服务：认证服务提供者的附加功能

**法规出处**：韩国《ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE ACT》第18条【来源3】。

**深度解读**：该条允许认证服务提供者应订阅者或使用者请求，以其电子签名验证电子文件**提交至该提供者之时点**。这实质上提供了“时间戳”式的时点证明机制，虽条文简短，但对电子签名的效力认定具有实务价值：签署时点往往关系到意思表示是否成立、是否在授权期限内、是否存在事后篡改等争点。由独立认证服务提供者验证时点，可增强电子文件证据链的完整性。

**重点提示**：该服务以“请求”为前提，非认证服务提供者的法定义务；验证的是“提交时点”，而非签名生成时点，二者在争议中可能被区分质证。

**实务指引**：对时效敏感的交易（如投标、要约承诺、期限届满前通知），建议主动请求认证服务提供者进行时点验证并留存记录；在诉讼中可将该记录与签名验证结果结合使用，形成完整证据链。

### 5. 跨法域比较视角下的异同（基于现有资料的范围说明）

**法规出处**：韩国《ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE ACT》第3条、第4条【来源4】【来源2】。

**深度解读**：从现有资料看，韩国法的鲜明特点是：**效力认定采功能等同、不因电子形式否定**（第3条），**类型划分以定义与认证体系为主、未在条文层面明示分级效力**（第2条），并以**政府政策义务**保障可靠性与国际互认（第4条）。这与部分法域将电子签名明确区分为“简单/高级/合格”并分别配置效力推定与举证责任的立法模式形成对照；但关于其他法域的具体类型划分与效力规则，现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定，不宜在此作确定性比较结论。

**重点提示**：跨境场景下，不能仅凭韩国法第3条的“同等效力”推定其在另一法域当然有效；应结合对方法域对签名形式、认证等级与互认安排的具体要求判断。

**实务指引**：跨境合同宜设置“电子签名条款”，明确适用法、认可的签名类型与认证标准，并约定时点验证与证据保存方式；对高价值交易，优先采用经认证的签名并保留证书与验证报告，降低跨法域举证成本。

## 三、总结与建议

韩国《电子签名法》以**功能等同**为核心认定电子签名效力，明确不得仅因电子形式否定其作为手写签名或签名盖章的效力，并在法令或协议选定情形下赋予同等效力（第3条）【来源4】；其类型划分依托第2条的定义体系与认证、证书制度【来源1】，并通过第4条政府政策义务保障可靠性、互操作性与国际互认【来源2】，第18条则提供时点验证的辅助机制【来源3】。行动上，建议：第一，在合同中明确电子签名类型与认证要求；第二，对时效敏感文件主动做时点验证；第三，跨境交易先核查对方法域的效力规则与互认安排。延伸提醒：认证服务提供者的资质与责任、签名生成数据的保管安全、以及争议中证据链的完整性，均是效力落地时的关键风险点。

## 一、核心概括

亚太各法域对金融科技并无统一监管范式，而是呈现“功能监管、牌照准入、风险防控、反洗钱合规”四条主线并行的格局。新加坡以统一立法整合金融科技牌照与数字代币服务监管，中国大陆以机构牌照与信息科技风险管理为抓手，美国则以跨境账户申报和反洗钱合规实现穿透式监管。以下结合五部法规逐一解读。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 新加坡：以统一立法整合金融科技与数字代币服务监管

**法规出处**：新加坡《Financial Services and Markets Act 2022》第1部分释义条款及生效安排【来源1】。

**深度解读**：该法是一部“金融 sector-wide”的综合性立法，其立法意图在于将原本分散于《证券与期货法》《支付服务法》等法规中的监管事项整合为统一框架。从释义条款看，“financial institution”的定义明确涵盖依《支付服务法2019》持牌的主体、依本法持牌提供**数字代币服务**的主体，以及依其他 MAS scheduled Act 受监管的主体【来源1】。这意味着金融科技企业一旦涉足支付或数字代币业务，即被纳入“金融机构”范畴，适用统一的审慎监管、行为监管与处置机制。该法还分阶段生效（2022年至2025年），体现监管者对数字代币等新兴业态采取“逐步落地、分步实施”的审慎态度。

**重点提示**：数字代币服务提供商的牌照义务自2025年6月30日起随第9部分生效【来源1】，企业须关注生效时间节点，避免在过渡期内无牌经营。此外，被豁免持牌的主体仍可能被纳入“金融机构”定义（定义(q)(i)项明确包括豁免主体），豁免不等于免于监管。

**实务指引**：拟进入新加坡市场的金融科技企业，应首先对照“financial institution”定义逐项自查是否落入(a)至(q)任一类别；涉及数字代币服务的，须提前向MAS申请牌照并建立合规体系；建议建立法规生效时间跟踪机制，按各Part生效日期分阶段完成合规改造。

### 2. 美国：以跨境账户申报制度实现穿透式反洗钱监管

**法规出处**：美国《Bank Secrecy Act Regulations》31 CFR 1010.350【来源2】。

**深度解读**：该条要求“United States person”对在外国持有的银行、证券或其他金融账户具有**财务利益**或**签字权**时，须按年度向国税局局长申报（即FBAR制度）。其核心在于“穿透”——不仅账户名义持有人须申报，通过代理人、 nominee、持股超50%的 corporation、特定信托等间接持有账户的，同样视为具有财务利益【来源2】。反避税条款更进一步：为规避申报而设立实体的，该实体持有的账户仍归责于设立人。这一制度对跨境金融科技企业影响深远：凡美国主体在亚太地区开立或控制账户，均可能触发申报义务。

**重点提示**：签字权（signature or other authority）的认定标准是“有权通过直接沟通控制资金处置”，即便无财务利益也可能触发申报；但银行、受SEC/CFTC监管机构等的雇员在无财务利益时可豁免【来源2】。持有25个以上账户的可适用简化申报规则。

**实务指引**：跨境金融科技企业应建立账户台账，逐一识别美国主体（公民、居民、在美设立实体）的境外账户及签字权安排；对通过代理人或子公司持有的账户进行穿透核查；每年按时提交FBAR，并保留支持性文件至少五年。常见误区是认为“公司账户由公司申报即可”，忽视个人签字权的独立申报义务。

### 3. 中国大陆：以机构牌照准入与信息科技风险管理双轨并行

**法规出处**：中国大陆《银行保险机构许可证管理办法》第2条【来源5】；《汽车金融公司管理办法》第47条【来源3】。

**深度解读**：中国大陆对金融科技相关业务的监管采取“牌照先行”模式。第2条明确，许可证是金融监管总局依法颁发的**特许**银行保险机构经营金融业务的法律文件，颁发、换发、收缴等职权由金融监管总局及其授权派出机构专属行使，其他任何单位和个人不得行使【来源5】。这确立了金融业务特许经营的基本立场——未持牌即不得经营。与此同时，《汽车金融公司管理办法》第47条要求汽车金融公司建立与信息系统运行管理模式相匹配的**信息科技风险管理体系**，强化网络安全、数据安全、业务连续性、外包等领域风险防控【来源3】。两条规定形成“准入+持续运营”的双层结构：牌照解决“能不能做”，信息科技风控解决“做得是否稳健”。

**重点提示**：许可证职权具有排他性，任何声称可“代办”“协调”许可证的第三方均不具合法性；信息科技风险管理是持牌机构的持续性义务，外包并不转移主体责任。

**实务指引**：金融科技企业若涉足银行保险或汽车金融业务，须先取得相应许可证，再搭建信息科技风险管理体系；建议将网络安全、数据安全、业务连续性、外包管理四项作为独立风控模块，制定应急预案并定期演练；对拟合作的外包服务商开展尽职调查，明确责任边界。

### 4. 泰国：以反洗钱上游犯罪清单界定金融合规边界

**法规出处**：泰国《Money Laundering Control Act, 1999》第3条【来源4】。

**深度解读**：该条以释义方式界定了“predicate offence”（上游犯罪）、“transaction”“suspicious transaction”“financial institution”等核心概念。上游犯罪清单涵盖毒品、性犯罪、公共欺诈、侵占诈骗、渎职、敲诈勒索、走私等【来源4】。“suspicious transaction”的定义尤为宽泛：与同类交易性质不同、缺乏经济合理性、合理怀疑为规避本法而进行、或与上游犯罪有关联的交易，无论次数多寡均属之【来源4】。“financial institution”则涵盖泰国央行、商业银行、金融公司、证券公司、人寿及非人寿保险公司、储蓄合作社及部级规章规定的其他金融业务法人【来源4】。金融科技企业若落入“financial institution”范围，即须履行可疑交易报告等反洗钱义务。

**重点提示**：可疑交易的判断标准不要求交易已被证实与犯罪有关，“可能有关联”即可触发报告义务；规避本法适用的交易本身即被推定为可疑，企业不得设计交易结构以规避申报。

**实务指引**：在泰展业的金融科技企业应首先确认是否属于“financial institution”定义范围；建立可疑交易监测系统，重点识别缺乏经济合理性、结构异常复杂、疑似拆分规避的交易；制定内部报告流程并对员工开展反洗钱培训；对上游犯罪清单进行定期更新跟踪。

### 5. 跨法域比较：监管模式的共同点与差异点

**深度解读**：从五部法规看，亚太金融科技监管存在三项共同逻辑：其一，**准入控制**——新加坡以牌照整合、中国大陆以许可证特许、美国以申报义务实现主体识别；其二，**风险为本**——中国大陆强调信息科技风险，泰国强调可疑交易监测，美国强调账户穿透；其三，**穿透与实质**——美国反避税条款、泰国可疑交易定义、新加坡对豁免主体的纳入，均体现“不看形式看实质”的监管取向。差异在于：新加坡采统一立法模式，中国大陆采分业牌照模式，美国采申报合规模式，泰国采反洗钱义务模式，严格程度与适用对象各有侧重。

**重点提示**：同一金融科技业务在多个法域可能同时触发不同义务（如新加坡牌照+美国FBAR+泰国反洗钱报告），企业须做多法域合规映射，而非择一适用。

**实务指引**：建议企业制作“法域—义务”矩阵表，列明各法域的准入要求、持续合规义务、报告时限与责任主体；对跨境账户、数字代币、支付服务等高频交叉领域设置专项合规负责人。

## 三、总结与建议

**多法域对比简表**：

| 法域 | 监管模式 | 核心抓手 | 严格程度特征 |
|------|----------|----------|--------------|
| 新加坡 | 统一立法+牌照 | 数字代币服务牌照、金融机构统一定义 | 分阶段生效，审慎渐进 |
| 美国 | 申报合规+穿透 | FBAR账户申报、反避税条款 | 穿透至个人签字权，申报义务独立 |
| 中国大陆 | 分业牌照+持续风控 | 许可证特许、信息科技风险管理 | 准入排他性强，运营义务持续 |
| 泰国 | 反洗钱义务 | 上游犯罪清单、可疑交易报告 | 定义宽泛，预防性报告义务重 |

**总结**：亚太金融科技监管不存在单一模式，而是准入、申报、风控、反洗钱多线并行。新加坡的统一立法适合作为区域总部架构设计的参照，美国的穿透申报对跨境账户安排提出高要求，中国大陆的牌照特许与信息科技风控强调持牌经营与稳健运营，泰国的反洗钱框架则要求交易层面的持续监测。

**行动指引**：企业进入亚太市场前，应先完成“业务类型—法域—义务”三维映射，再决定牌照申请、账户架构与监测系统的优先次序。

**延伸提醒**：其一，新加坡数字代币服务牌照义务2025年6月30日生效，须提前布局；其二，美国FBAR的签字权申报独立于财务利益，个人层面易被遗漏；其三，泰国可疑交易报告以“可能关联”为门槛，合规系统不宜设置过高触发阈值。

**说明**：关于各法域金融科技沙盒、跨境数据流动等具体制度，现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定，建议另行检索各监管机构发布的配套规则。

## 一、核心概括

亚太各国数据泄露通知义务在触发条件上普遍以"可能造成个人权益损害"或"未经授权访问/泄露"为核心门槛，通知时限则从"立即"到"60日"不等，差异显著。但需特别说明：**现有参考资料库仅包含美国联邦法规（HIPAA、FCRA关联规则、GLBA保障规则）及少量日本法条摘录，未提供亚太各国（如中国、新加坡、澳大利亚、韩国等）数据泄露通知义务的完整法规原文**，因此本回答将基于资料库中可用的美国法域规则及日本法条摘录进行有限度的比较分析，并明确指出资料不足之处。


## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 美国HIPAA：60日硬性上限与"发现"标准

**法规出处**：美国《HIPAA - Security and Privacy》第164.404条(b)款、第164.410条(b)款、第164.406条(b)款【来源1】【来源3】【来源4】。

**深度解读**：HIPAA体系对数据泄露通知设定了**三层通知义务**——向受影响个人（164.404）、向媒体（164.406，涉及500人以上本州居民时）、以及商业伙伴向覆盖实体（164.410）。三者的时限规则高度统一：**"不得无故延迟，且在任何情况下不得超过发现泄露后60个日历日"** 。关键在于"发现"（discovery）的认定标准：第164.404条(a)(2)款规定，泄露视为在覆盖实体**已知或通过合理勤勉应当已知**的第一天即被发现；且任何员工或代理人在非泄露实施者身份下知悉，即视为实体知悉。这一"归责式知悉"标准意味着企业不能以"管理层尚未汇报"为由拖延计时。

**重点提示**：60日是**上限而非目标**，监管机构期望在合理时间内尽快通知；若执法机构认定通知会妨碍刑事调查，可依第164.412条延迟。商业伙伴（business associate）的60日起算点独立于覆盖实体，且须在通知中尽可能识别每位受影响个人【来源3】。

**实务指引**：企业应建立**内部泄露发现日志**，记录"最早知悉时间"而非"确认时间"；在商业伙伴协议中明确约定对方发现后须在X日内（建议不超过10日）通知己方，以保留自身60日窗口的操作空间；准备标准化通知模板，涵盖第164.404条(c)款要求的五项要素（事件描述、信息类型、个人防护建议、实体应对措施、联系方式）。

### 2. 美国PHR供应商规则：30日FTC通知与500人媒体门槛

**法规出处**：美国《Exemption for Affiliates from Fair Credit Reporting Act》第318.3条(a)款【来源2】；《Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information》第314.4条(j)款【来源5】。

**深度解读**：针对个人健康记录（PHR）供应商及PHR相关实体，第318.3条要求其在发现泄露后通知受影响个人、**联邦贸易委员会（FTC）** ，以及在涉及某州500名以上居民时通知**主流媒体**。值得注意的是，第314.4条(j)(1)款（GLBA保障规则）对金融机构设定了更严格的FTC通知时限：涉及**至少500名消费者**时，须"尽快且不迟于发现后30日"以电子方式向FTC报告。这与HIPAA的60日形成对比，体现了不同法域对通知时限的差异化设计。

**重点提示**：PHR供应商与HIPAA覆盖实体的通知对象不同——前者须直接通知FTC，后者主要通过卫生与公众服务部（HHS）报告。第318.3条(b)款还要求**第三方服务提供商**向供应商书面指定官员发出通知并**取得回执**，这是供应链合规的关键节点。

**实务指引**：涉及健康数据的平台企业应首先判定自身属于HIPAA覆盖实体、商业伙伴还是PHR供应商，三者通知路径和时限不同；建立**FTC电子通知表单**的预填机制；与第三方服务商合同中明确"发现即通知+回执确认"条款。

### 3. 日本法条摘录：资料有限，仅见程序性规定

**法规出处**：日本《Act on the Protection of Personal Information》第84条【知识图谱关联】。

**深度解读**：资料库中仅摘录了日本法第84条关于**披露决定期限的例外**（大量个人信息披露请求可能严重妨碍事务时），该条并非直接规定数据泄露通知的触发条件或时限。知识图谱关联显示日本法第84、85条涉及"通知义务"，但**摘录内容未包含泄露通知的具体时限和触发要件**。因此，关于日本《个人信息保护法》下泄露通知义务的完整规则（如2022年修正后引入的"可能造成财产损失或人格权益损害"触发标准及"速报"义务），**现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定**，无法据此作出准确比较。

**重点提示**：不得基于知识图谱的"通知义务"标签推断日本法的具体时限；实务中应另行查阅日本个人信息保护委员会（PPC）的指南。

**实务指引**：如企业涉及日本市场，建议单独委托当地律师核查PPC《个人信息保护法指南》中关于泄露报告的"速报"（通常要求知悉后3-5日内初步报告）规则，本资料库不足以支撑该结论。

### 4. 亚太比较的局限性说明与可用参照

**法规出处**：资料库整体范围【来源1-5】及知识图谱关联。

**深度解读**：用户问题涉及"亚太各国"，但资料库实质内容以**美国联邦法规**为主，辅以日本法两条摘录。知识图谱中虽出现《Act on the Protection of Personal Information》第84、85条及台湾地区《个人资料保护法》第21条的"通知义务"关联，但**均无条文原文支撑具体时限与触发条件**。因此，严谨的比较结论只能是：美国HIPAA体系以"发现后60日"为上限、以"未经授权访问/泄露+合理相信已发生"为触发；PHR/GLBA体系对FTC报告设30日时限、以500人为媒体通知门槛。亚太其他法域的具体规则，**现有资料暂未提供**。

**重点提示**：跨法域合规不能以美国规则类推亚太；各国触发条件（如新加坡PDPA的"显著损害"评估、澳大利亚NDB的"严重损害"门槛）需逐法域核实。

**实务指引**：建议企业制作**法域矩阵表**，逐国列明：触发标准（损害门槛/数量门槛）、通知对象（个人/监管/媒体）、时限（小时/日）、豁免情形（执法调查/补救措施），并标注每项的法律依据来源，避免以单一法域规则覆盖全球。

### 5. 通知内容与方式的共性要求

**法规出处**：第164.404条(c)(d)款【来源1】、第318.3条【来源2】。

**深度解读**：尽管时限各异，美国两部法规在**通知内容**上高度趋同：均要求以**通俗语言**说明事件、信息类型、个人防护措施、实体应对措施及联系方式【来源1】；通知方式以**书面一等邮件**为原则，电子邮件仅在个人同意时可用；联系信息不足时，10人以下可用替代方式，10人以上须**网站显著公告90日或主流媒体公告**并保留至少90日免费电话【来源1】。这些程序性要求可作为亚太合规文书设计的参照模板。

**重点提示**：替代通知的"10人分界"和"90日"是硬性程序指标，容易在实务中被忽略。

**实务指引**：预先设计多层级通知渠道（邮件/网站/媒体/电话热线），并在事件响应预案中明确触发替代通知的判定流程。


## 三、总结与建议

综合现有资料，可确认的美国法域规则是：HIPAA对个人通知设**发现后60日上限**、以"未经授权访问或泄露且合理相信已发生"为触发；PHR/GLBA体系对FTC报告设**30日**时限、以**500名消费者**为媒体通知门槛；通知内容须通俗、含五项要素，方式以书面为原则。**关于亚太各国（除日本有限摘录外）的具体时限与触发条件，现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定**，本回答无法给出跨国比较的确定结论。

**行动建议**：第一，切勿以美国60日规则类推亚太法域，应逐国核查当地个人信息保护法及监管指南；第二，建立"最早知悉时间"记录机制，因为多数法域的时限均从"发现"起算；第三，将通知内容模板与替代通知程序标准化，以应对不同法域的程序要求。

**延伸提醒**：日本法第84条摘录仅涉披露期限例外，不构成泄露通知规则，需另行核实PPC指南；知识图谱中的"通知义务"关联仅为辅助佐证，不得替代条文原文；跨境业务建议按法域制作合规矩阵并定期更新。

164.404 Notification to individuals.
(a)
Standard
—(1)
General rule.
A covered entity shall, following the discovery of a breach of unsecured protected health information, notify each individual whose unsecured protected health information has been, or is reasonably believed by the covered entity to have been, accessed, acquired, used, or disclosed as a result of such breach.
(2)
Breaches treated as discovered.
For purposes of
paragraph (a)(1)
of this section,
§§ 164.406(a)
, and


164.408(a)
, a breach shall be treated as discovered by a covered entity as of the first day on which such breach is known to the covered entity, or, by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known to the covered entity. A covered entity shall be deemed to have knowledge of a breach if such breach is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to any person, other than the person committing the breach, who is a workforce member or agent of the covered entity (determined in accordance with the federal common law of agency).


(b)
Implementation specification: ss of notification.
Except as provided in
§ 164.412
, a covered entity shall provide the notification required by
paragraph (a)
of this section without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery of a breach.
(c)
Implementation specifications: Content of notification
—(1)
Elements.
The notification required by
paragraph (a)
of this section shall include, to the extent possible:
(A)
A brief description of what happened, including the date of the breach and the date of the discovery of the breach, if known;


(B)
A description of the types of unsecured protected health information that were involved in the breach (such as whether full name, social security number, date of birth, address, account number, diagnosis, disability code, or other types of information were involved);
(C)
Any steps individuals should take to protect themselves from potential harm resulting from the breach;
(D)
A brief description of what the covered entity involved is doing to investigate the breach, to mitigate harm to individuals, and to protect against any further breaches; and


(E)
Contact procedures for individuals to ask questions or learn additional information, which shall include a toll-free telephone number, an e-mail address, Web site, or postal address.
(2)
Plain language requirement.
The notification required by
paragraph (a)
of this section shall be written in plain language.
(d)
Implementation specifications: Methods of individual notification.
The notification required by
paragraph (a)
of this section shall be provided in the following form:
(1)
Written notice.


(i) Written notification by first-class mail to the individual at the last known address of the individual or, if the individual agrees to electronic notice and such agreement has not been withdrawn, by electronic mail. The notification may be provided in one or more mailings as information is available.


(ii) If the covered entity knows the individual is deceased and has the address of the next of kin or personal representative of the individual (as specified under
§ 164.502(g)(4)
of E), written notification by first-class mail to either the next of kin or personal representative of the individual. The notification may be provided in one or more mailings as information is available.


(2)
Substitute notice.
In the case in which there is insufficient or out-of-date contact information that precludes written notification to the individual under
paragraph (d)(1)(i)
of this section, a substitute form of notice reasonably calculated to reach the individual shall be provided. Substitute notice need not be provided in the case in which there is insufficient or out-of-date contact information that precludes written notification to the next of kin or personal representative of the individual under paragraph (d)(1)(ii).


(i) In the case in which there is insufficient or out-of-date contact information for fewer than 10 individuals, then such substitute notice may be provided by an alternative form of written notice, telephone, or other means.
(ii) In the case in which there is insufficient or out-of-date contact information for 10 or more individuals, then such substitute notice shall:
(A)
Be in the form of either a conspicuous posting for a period of 90 days on the page of the Web site of the covered entity involved, or conspicuous notice in major print or broadcast media in geographic areas where the individuals affected by the breach likely reside; and


(B)
Include a toll-free phone number that remains active for at least 90 days where an individual can learn whether the individual's unsecured protected health information may be included in the breach.
(3)
Additional notice in urgent situations.
In any case deemed by the covered entity to require urgency because of possible imminent misuse of unsecured protected health information, the covered entity may provide information to individuals by telephone or other means, as appropriate, in addition to notice provided under
paragraph (d)(1)
of this section.

318.3 Breach notification requirement.
(a)
In general.
In accordance with
§§ 318.4
(regarding ss of notification), 318.5 (regarding methods of notice), and 318.6 (regarding content of notice), each vendor of personal health records, following the discovery of a breach of security of unsecured PHR identifiable health information that is in a personal health record maintained or offered by such vendor, and each PHR related entity, following the discovery of a breach of security of such information that is obtained through a product or service provided by such entity, shall:
(1)
Notify each individual who is a citizen or resident of the United States whose unsecured PHR identifiable health information was acquired by an unauthorized person as a result of such breach of security;


(2)
Notify the Federal Trade Commission; and
(3)
Notify prominent media outlets serving a State or jurisdiction, following the discovery of a breach of security, if the unsecured PHR identifiable health information of 500 or more residents of such State or jurisdiction is, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired during such breach.

(b)
Third party service providers.
A third party service provider shall, following the discovery of a breach of security, provide notice of the breach to an official designated in a written contract by the vendor of personal health records or the PHR related entity to receive such notices or, if such a designation is not made, to a senior official at the vendor of personal health records or PHR related entity to which it provides services, and obtain acknowledgment from such official that such notice was received. Such notification shall include the identification of each customer of the vendor of personal health records or PHR related entity whose unsecured PHR identifiable health information has been, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired during such breach.

 For purposes of ensuring implementation of this
paragraph (b)
, vendors of personal health records and PHR related entities shall notify third party service providers of their status as vendors of personal health records or PHR related entities subject to this part. While some third party service providers may access unsecured PHR identifiable health information in the course of providing services, this does not render the third party service provider a PHR related entity.

(c)
Breaches treated as discovered.
A breach of security shall be treated as discovered as of the first day on which such breach is known or reasonably should have been known to the vendor of personal health records, PHR related entity, or third party service provider, respectively. Such vendor, entity, or third party service provider shall be deemed to have knowledge of a breach if such breach is known, or reasonably should have been known, to any person, other than the person committing the breach, who is an employee, officer, or other agent of such vendor of personal health records, PHR related entity, or third party service provider.

Standard

paragraph (a)(1)

§ 164.412
, a business associate shall provide the notification required by

paragraph (a)
of this section shall include, to the extent possible, the identification of each individual whose unsecured protected health information has been, or is reasonably believed by the business associate to have been, accessed, acquired, used, or disclosed during the breach.
